title: Arranging and the origins of the Dawn Busters at WWL
summary: He started writing arrangements early. Ray Benitez's rehearsal band with Pinky Vidakovich fronting became the WWL staff band, the Dawn Busters, and ran until 1959.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Uh, Fred Lloyd Cantor read pretty good on guitar. In the sax section, we were all side readers. Uh-huh. When did you start writing? I don't know. I always liked it. And, uh, I, I could never play piano, but I would use a piano just to, to sound chords. I still can't play. I can just make a chord if I studied my fingers long enough. But, uh, I would say, within five years from the time I started, I just liked it. It was a creative thing that I liked, you know, that you could write something and make people play it. Which band did you write the most for? Oh, the Dawn Busters. Dawn Busters? Oh, for years I, with the acceptance of stocks, I wrote practically everything that they had. And, uh, well, that, that's another long, almost dull story where the Dawn Busters came from. Well, Boris. Boring band. No, it wasn't a boring band. It wasn't, far from being a boring band. It was, it was the results of guys who liked to play music. And the driving spirit, I must say, was Ray Benitez. Yeah. Because Ray Benitez organized what was nothing but a rehearsal band. We used to do it mostly in the studios at WSMB, way up on the 13th floor of the Maison Blanche building, with no idea of getting a job. And I wrote some orchestrations, Johnny Ronigan wrote some, and we'd rehearse like mad. And at that time, I was living on charters near St. Rock and Nina, Johnny Ronigan, and myself would get together and just play saxophone things. I'd write some, Johnny would write some, we'd make a little look at a stock, just try to blend and all. You know, none of us ever got tired. We'd play it six hours at home and go play a four hour job. This was fine. And the genesis of that was that Ray was trying to promote the job at what was then the Beverly Gardens, or suburban gardens, I'm sorry, later it was the Beverly Gardens. And he finally succeeded, but they told him we'd need somebody to counter front the band, because they were, it was a gambling house and they wanted to, you know, an actual guy to stay in the front of the band. And Ray decided on Pinky Vidakovich. He had a lot of personality, he had a lot of friends. And so Pinky at that time was playing in Memphis, we were rehearsing in WSMP. And finally the, the job in Memphis collapsed and Pinky came home. And so all he had to do was go out with Ray to, to talk to the owners of the place. And we got the job out there as this band. We lasted out there about six weeks. And then the club collapsed. I don't know whether we helped it to collapse or what. But this became the nucleus for the Dawn Busters, this exact same band. When WWL decided that they wanted a staff band, they hired us to go in there. And the, the only difference is that we added a violin, because I don't know why exactly, but the violin became a part of the band. But this is where the Dawn Busters came from. We were the WWL staff at that time. And then years later when they decided that they wanted to try to change, change something different, the Dawn Busters went on as a morning feature. But we were on the air at WWL, I guess about, oh, three or four or five years. I don't even remember how long off the top of my head. As a staff band, we played three times a day at 10.30, 12.30, and 5.30. 30-minute programs. And on Sunday we did a concert.
We're talking about the early and mid-30s now, are we?
I would say about 19, 20. Yes, you're right. Yes, it would have been 32, something like that.
Well, how long did the Dawn Busters last then?

The Dawn Busters itself would have been, I think, I'm trusting memory for a minute, somewhere around 41, 42. They stopped in 41 or 42? No, we started. We started. We started. We went off the air as Dawn Busters in 59. And then I left the station in 60. And then I left the station in 60. But I was with the station altogether for 27 years. But the Dawn Busters, as the Dawn Busters, this was the same band really.
Oh, who was the violinist that you had?
